session_covered: US and European sessions of Friday 9 October
intro: Covers the Friday 9 October US/European session (US markets reopen after the weekend later today). SPI 200 futures and the VIX could not be verified from reliable sources and are shown as "not available".
footnotes: Index closes, yield and Brent from AP; AUD/USD, gold and iron ore from Trading Economics only (single source). Iron ore is a CFD benchmark tracking 62% Fe CFR Tianjin, not an official CFR China print.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures level and change: not available (no verified source), so the implied open is not calculated. Prior ASX 200 close (Fri 9 Oct): 8,717, +56 points (+0.6%), +0.4% for the week. Wall Street's gains and a weaker US dollar are mildly supportive.

what_moved: US stocks rose on expectations of a strong earnings season, leaving the S&P 500 about 0.4% below its record high. Oil eased early after President Trump said the US would not strike Iran before the midterms, but Brent reversed to close higher. Treasury yields stayed near a 24-year high. S&P 500 sector performance was not reported by the sources found. France, Germany and the UK each gained at least 1%.

news.headline: Fed hike pricing.
news.summary: Markets see about an 81-82% chance of a hold in October and a high chance of a hike by December, after last month's hike.

news.headline: Yields near 24-year high.
news.summary: The US 10-year is 5.24%, close to its highest since 2002; strong 10- and 30-year auction demand limited the rise.

news.headline: US consumer inflation expectations rise.
news.summary: Consumers expect 4.7% inflation over the next year, up from 4.6% a month earlier.

news.headline: Iran uncertainty keeps oil above US$100.
news.summary: Brent settled at US$104.72 as markets weigh when war-related disruption to energy supply will ease.

news.headline: SpaceX spectrum deal jolts US telecoms.
news.summary: T-Mobile US fell 13.3%, AT&T 9.8% and Verizon 8.7%, while tower operators rallied sharply.

news.headline: Australian labour market softening.
news.summary: Unemployment rose to 4.6% in August; markets price about a 30% chance of another RBA hike in November after the cash rate rose to 4.60% last month.

news.headline: US bank earnings start Tuesday.
news.summary: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo report; S&P 500 Q3 earnings are expected to rise over 30%.

coming_up: Tue 13 Oct: US big-bank earnings. Wed 14 Oct: US September CPI (consensus 3.6% y/y headline). Thu 15 Oct: Australian September employment report and US PPI.
